drivingQuestion: Does R' Elazar b. R' Shimon permit because he rejects muktze like his father?

segments.he: וְאֵין מַנְהִיגִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בַּמַּקֵּל בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר. לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כַּאֲבוּהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה? לָא, בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה, מִשּׁוּם דְּמִחֲזֵי כְּמַאן דְּאָזֵיל לְחִנְגָּא.
segments.en: The baraita continues: «And one may not lead an animal with a stick on a Festival, but Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permits» it. The Gemara asks: «Shall we say» that «Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, holds in accordance with» the opinion of «his father,» Rabbi Shimon, «who is not» of the opinion that there is a prohibition of «muktze,» and he therefore permits one to take any stick and lead an animal with it? The Gemara rejects this: «No,» there is no issue of muktze here at all, for in «this» case «even Rabbi Shimon concedes» to the first tanna that this activity is prohibited, not due to muktze but «because» one who does so «looks like one who is going to the market [ḥinga]» in the manner of a weekday. On a Festival, one must therefore lead the animal in an unusual fashion.
